question: What claim about efficacy is being made by attributing result to mere knowledge that has been heard, addressed to one of fair face?
premises: An instrument is indicated by a demonstrative.
That instrument is characterized as mere knowledge and as what has been heard.
The address is made to one of fair face.
inference: Mere knowledge, when heard, is presented here as sufficient by the means indicated.
uncertainties: The specific result produced is not stated in this verse.
plain_english: By this mere knowledge, by what has been heard, O fair-faced one.
